name: Bezalel
bio:
Bezalel is the grandson of Hur and son of Uri of the tribe of Judah, personally called by name by the LORD to serve as the chief craftsman for building the tabernacle (Exodus 31:1-5; 35:30-33). God filled him with the Spirit, giving him wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of craftsmanship — gold, silver, and bronze work, cutting and setting stones, and carving wood — making him the first person in Scripture explicitly described as being "filled with the Spirit of God" for a skilled craft.

Bezalel was also given the gift of teaching others, working alongside Oholiab of the tribe of Dan to train other skilled craftsmen in completing the tabernacle, all its furnishings, the sanctuary's equipment, and the priestly garments (Exodus 35:30-35; 36-39). His name means "in the shadow of God," fittingly capturing that all his craftsmanship flowed from wisdom God Himself gave him.

Generations later, the bronze altar Bezalel had made was still in use at the tabernacle's resting place in Gibeon, where Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on it the night God appeared to him and granted him wisdom (2 Chronicles 1:5-6).
